 Centre Raises Diesel, ATF Export Levies; Petrol Duty Unchanged 
 19 Nov 2026 
 2 Min Read 
 CW Team 
 Share 
 -->
 The Centre has raised the export levy on diesel to Rs. 14 per litre and the duty on aviation turbine fuel (ATF) to Rs. 12.5 per litre, marking the second increase in less than three weeks. The revisions form part of the government’s continuing review of petroleum product export duties amid geopolitical uncertainty.
 Notifications issued by the Finance Ministry said the special additional excise duty (SAED) on diesel exports had increased from Rs. 11.5 to Rs. 14 per litre. The levy on ATF exports has risen from Rs. 11 to Rs. 12.5 per litre. The export duty on petrol remains nil, with both SAED and the Road and Infrastructure Cess (RIC) continuing at zero.
 The revised rates took effect on November 16, following an earlier revision on October 31. At that time, the government raised the diesel export levy from Rs. 8.5 to Rs. 11.5 per litre and the ATF duty from Rs. 10.5 to Rs. 11 per litre, while removing the Rs. 2.5 per litre levy on petrol exports.
 Export levies on petrol, diesel and ATF were introduced on March 27, 2026, to support domestic availability by discouraging overseas sales amid the West Asia crisis. The rates are reviewed every fortnight and are based on average international prices for crude oil, petrol, diesel and ATF during the period since the previous review. The latest changes apply only to exports, with no alteration to excise duties on petrol and diesel supplied for domestic consumption. The fortnightly mechanism enables the Centre to adjust export levies in response to international fuel price movements while seeking to maintain adequate supplies in the domestic market.
